title: About
bio: Banyi Huang (they/them) is an artist working across multiple systems: digital bodies in virtual environments, sculptural devices, installation and performance.

They turn to the reenactment of mythology as a framework for connecting with ancestors and their physio-spiritual attributes–recognizing within that the self that generated a version of that lineage has already become an ancestor.

Core to the artist’s practice, cycles of return bridges the technical and the bodily across time. The process of sculpting reconfigurable bodies, building node-based animation systems, and fabricating ritual objects is inherently iterative. They turn technical repetition into a sustained form of attention, and through time, cultivate a practice of devotion.

Currently, Banyi is investigating live performance as a system in which the body, translated through devotional incantations and gestures, acts as a direct animation input. They are currently a second-year graduate student at UCLA’s Design Media Art program.
